sources.entry: toolz - A collection of functional utilities for iterators, functions, and dictionaries. Also available as cytoolz for Cython-accelerated performance.

summary.one_liner: toolz is a pure-Python library of functional utilities for iterables, functions, and dictionaries, with a Cython-accelerated drop-in counterpart called cytoolz.
summary.what_it_does: Provides helpers split into three modules: itertoolz for iterable operations (e.g. groupby, unique, interpose), functoolz for higher-order functions (e.g. memoize, curry, compose), and dicttoolz for dictionary operations (e.g. assoc, update-in, merge). The README shows composing functions such as compose, frequencies, and a curried map to build a word-count function. A curried submodule (toolz.curried) is available. The functions are described as coming from the legacy of functional list-processing languages. The library is pure Python with no dependencies beyond the standard library. The README says the project has been reimplemented in Cython as cytoolz, a drop-in replacement. API documentation is referenced externally.
use_cases: composing small functions into data pipelines
speeding up toolz with a Cython build
notable: Split into itertoolz, functoolz, and dicttoolz modules covering iterables, functions, and dicts
Pure Python with no dependencies beyond the standard library
cytoolz drop-in replacement for Cython-accelerated performance
Includes a curried namespace for use with compose and map pipelines
caveats: Project status is 'alive but inactive': maintainers only handle critical bug fixes, Python version bumps, and security issues, and review few contributions
Maintainers consider the library mostly complete, so new features are unlikely
